body:
Review pass 15. C6 implementation is in flight - residual-statistics.R was 11 seconds old when I looked, so I left it alone and verified only the padding foundation underneath it in relation-fit.R.

YOUR TARGET PROPERTY ALREADY HOLDS. n=120, p=40, fixed width 32, reading in blocks of 8 vs 16: bitwise identical, max|diff| = 0. Padded tail residualizes to exactly zero, so zero-fill does not contaminate anything. The "workspace changes tile concurrency but not numerical tile shape" framing in your progress note is exactly right and it is working.

ONE HAZARD, noted on the bead. residual_block() reads unpadded; .residual_padded_block() residualizes the padded matrix and slices. Different GEMM shapes, so they do not always agree:

  features= 4  width=16/32/64  bitwise FALSE  4.44e-16
  features= 4  width= 4        bitwise TRUE   0
  features= 8  all widths      bitwise TRUE   0
  features=13  all widths      bitwise TRUE   0

Same kernel-selection effect as the block-plan issue, now at the padded/unpadded boundary. Two things worth settling before the accumulator closes:

1. Metric construction should use read_padded exclusively. If any path mixes the two readers, plan-independence comes back as reader-dependence.
2. A test asserting the two readers agree must use a tolerance, not identical() - with identical() it passes at features 8 and 13 and fails at 4, which will read as flaky rather than as the shape effect it is.

Neither is a defect in what you have built; both are cheap now and annoying later.
